summary: The stack is justified: two measured T=1 wins on disjoint kernels (R and the unpooler slice), each -2.4 to -3.6 us against the control, adding up to about -4 to -6 us on decode_1 where err is ~0.6 us. The merge is easier than the brief fears: boundaries-unpooler-pdl-small-t is a separate TU (_DLB_CUDA / _DLB_EXT), and its patch applies cleanly on top of the route patch.
justification: Both source runs used the current master blob (base_blob 4da9467 = master:muse_decode_layer/submission.py), so their deltas are against today's BEST. Route: R 7.01 -> 5.79 us in prepare, decode_1 -3.4/-1.8 us vs BEST. Unpool NF=1: 6.5 vs 9.2 us. That gain is mostly intrinsic (it fuses the slice GEMM and the F.pad zero fill), and its predecessor (experts/combine) is unchanged. The only context change is the successor: the SGLang FFN boundary now launches normally instead of the PDL'd dl_boundary_kernel, so a ~0.5-1 us overlap may be lost. That is the weakest link, but it cannot flip the sign. Merge plan, verified in a scratch repo against the master blob: dl-route-warp-topk-pdl.patch applies clean, and boundaries-unpooler-pdl-small-t.patch then applies clean on top of it. Its CUDA lives in a second load_inline TU (_DLB_CPP/_DLB_CUDA, 'a second, separate TU'), so there is no _DL_CUDA conflict and no hand-port. The builder then removes the boundary half in kernel_fn. Expected shapes (decode_1 faster, verify_1 maybe, T>=9 flat) match the gates: NF=1 is T<=8, and the route change spans T<=32 but is only ~1 us there, inside err.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (master): both pieces live inside its PDL chain (P -> R -> experts). R's PDL wait depends on P issuing launch_dependents, which the route patch adds. If the chain were absent, neither gain would exist, but it is landed and unchanged.
stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 (master BEST): its side-stream dispatch is T>32 only, so it does not overlap at T<=8.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t (master): the Triton combine is the unpool kernel's PDL predecessor. It never triggers launch_dependents, so the unpool's pre-wait weight-ring prefetch overlaps only the combine's tail. That was the same in the boundaries run, so no new confound.

dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl-t1-gate (queued sibling): it also touches T=1 and edits _DL_CUDA (its patch does NOT apply on top of the route patch; it conflicts at the dl_pooler_router hunk ~line 295). Run both against master independently; whichever lands second hand-merges the _DL_CUDA TU.
interference: No companion. The two pieces are in separate kernels whose profile rows (dl_route_norm_align_kernel, and dl_unpool_kernel vs nvjet slice + pad) attribute each part in the same check. The decode_16/32 and verify_16/32 rows (T>=9, master unpooler) act as the drift control. Per-piece state flags let the self-check turn either off. A submit-grade A/B is the landing step, as the brief already says, not a companion.
rules_flags: The unpool's zero columns 1024..8191 must be written after griddepcontrol.wait, as the source kernel does, because the output buffer may be reused memory. Only weights may be read before the wait.
No other rules concerns: shape/config-only gates and prepare-time self-checks.
